newsitem.title: USA: Duke Power, PanEnergy to merge.
newsitem.headline: Duke Power, PanEnergy to merge.

text.p: Duke Power Co said on Monday that the boards of directors of Duke and PanEnergy Corp had approved a definitive agreement for a tax-free, stock-for-stock merger.
Under the agreement, each PanEnergy share would be converted into 1.0444 Duke shares, Duke said.
Based on Duke's closing price of $47.875 on November 22, Duke will issue about $7.7 billion in stock to PanEnergy stockholders to complete the transaction, it said.

PanEnergy stockholders will own about 44 percent of the common stock of the new company, which will have a market capitalization of about $23 billion, composed of $17 billion in equity and $6 billion in debt and preferred stock.

The transaction combines Duke, an investor-owned electric utility serving 1.8 million customers, with PanEnergy, an energy services company handling over 15 percent of the natural gas consumed in the United States.
At the deal's closing, Duke Power Co will change its name to Duke Energy Corp.
Upon completion of the merger, Richard Priory, currently president and chief operating officer of Duke, will become chairman and chief executive officer of Duke Energy.
Paul Anderson, president and CEO of PanEnergy, will become president and COO of the new company.
William Grigg, currently chairman and CEO of Duke, will retire.
Dennis Hendrix will step down as chairman of PanEnergy effective with the merger and will join Duke Energy's board, which will be made up of 18 members -- 11 from Duke and seven from PanEnergy.
Duke said it anticiaptes that the merger will become accretive to earnings at the end of the second year after completion of the deal.

Duke, which currently pays an annual dividend of $2.12 per share, said PanEnergy shareholders will receive an increase of $1.25 in dividends per share, based on the implied exchange ratio, from PanEnergy's current dividend of $0.96 per share.
After completion of the merger, PanEnergy will be a wholly-owned subsidiary of Duke Energy.
Duke Energy will be headquartered in Charlotte, N.C.
Houston will be the center for PanEnergy's pipeline operations, trading and marketing services, and certain business development activities.
The transaction is the biggest merger yet between an electric utility and a natural gas company and is part of a trend spurred by deregualtion.
In August, Houston Industries Inc and NorAm Energy Corp announced plans to merge in a transaction valued at $3.8 billion.
Under the Duke-PanEnergy merger agreement, no changes are required with respect to either company's public debt issues or the outstanding preferred stock of Duke.
The merger is subject to government regulatory procedures and approval by holders of a majority of PanEnergy common shares outstanding and a majority of Duke's common shares voting.
Duke said it believes the regulatory procedures can be completed in less than 12 months.
